chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The resident of Mecca, when he enters it for Umrah in the months other than Hajj (for indeed the months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah), if he enters it for Umrah in the months other than Hajj and then wishes to enter the state of Ihram (for Hajj), let him go out to Al-Ji'ranah, let him assume Ihram from there, then come to Mecca, and do not break the Talbiyah until he looks at the House, then he circles the House and prays two rak'ahs at the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), then he goes out to As-Safa and Al-Marwah and circles between them, then he shortens (his hair) and becomes free from Ihram, then he re-attaches the Talbiyah on the Day of Tarwiyah.
And the sick person, when he reaches the Miqat, let the one who is with him assume Ihram on his behalf, and he should avoid what the Muhrim avoids; he narrated that.

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةُ: Talbiyah (the recitation of 'Here I am, O God')
key_terms.الْمِيقَاتُ: Miqat (the designated boundary for assuming Ihram)
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for a resident of Mecca to perform Umrah and then Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific ritual protocol for a Mecca resident (Muqim) performing Umrah al-Mufrada outside the Hajj months, requiring them to exit to Al-Ji'ranah to renew Ihram for Hajj while maintaining continuous Talbiyah. It further addresses the practical accommodation for the sick, allowing a companion to assume Ihram on their behalf at the Miqat, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise adherence to boundaries (Mawaqit) and the flexibility of ritual obligations during illness.
